tree.heading: Consent to Multi-State Freight Mobility Compacts.—
tree.text: Congress recognizes the right of States, cities, regional planning organizations, federally recognized Indian Tribes, and local public authorities (including public port authorities) that are regionally linked with an interest in a specific nationally or regionally significant multi-State freight corridor to enter into multi-State compacts to promote the improved mobility of goods, including—

children.text: identifying projects along the corridor that benefit multiple States;
assembling rights-of-way; and
performing capital improvements.

tree.heading: Financing.—
tree.text: A multi-State freight compact established by entities under subsection (a) may provide that, in order to carry out the compact, the relevant States or other entities may—

children.text: accept contributions from a unit of State or local government;
use any Federal or State funds made available for freight mobility infrastructure planning or construction, including applying for grants;
subject to such terms and conditions as the States consider to be advisable—
borrow money on a short-term basis; and
issue—
notes for borrowing under subparagraph (A); and
bonds; and
obtain financing by other means permitted under applicable Federal or State law.

children.heading: In general.—
children.text: A multi-State freight compact under this section may establish a multi-State freight corridor advisory committee, which shall include representatives of State departments of transportation and other public and private sector entities with an interest in freight mobility, such as—
ports;
freight railroads;
shippers;
carriers;
freight-related associations;
third-party logistics providers;
the freight industry workforce;
environmental organizations;
community organizations; and
units of local government.

children.heading: Activities.—
children.text: An advisory committee established under paragraph (1) may—
advise the parties to the applicable multi-State freight compact with respect to freight-related priorities, issues, projects, and funding needs that impact multi-State—
freight mobility; and
supply chains;
serve as a forum for States, Indian Tribes, and other public entities to discuss decisions affecting freight mobility;
communicate and coordinate multi-State freight priorities with other organizations;
promote the sharing of information between the private and public sectors with respect to freight issues; and
provide information for consideration in the development of State freight plans under section 70202.

children.heading: Establishment.—
children.text: The Secretary of Transportation (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”) shall establish a program under which the Secretary shall provide grants to multi-State freight compacts, or States seeking to form a multi-State freight compact, that seek to improve a route or corridor that is a part of the National Multimodal Freight Network established under section 70103.

children.heading: In general.—
children.text: To incentivize the establishment of multi-State freight compacts, the Secretary may award a grant for operations costs in an amount of not more than $2,000,000 to—
a multi-State freight compact established under subsection (a) during the 2-year period beginning on the date of establishment of the multi-State freight compact; or
States seeking to form a multi-State freight compact described in that subsection.

children.heading: New multi-state freight compacts.—
children.text: A multi-State freight compact shall be eligible for a grant under this paragraph only during the initial 2 years of operation of the compact.

children.heading: States seeking to form a compact.—
children.text: States seeking to form a multi-State freight compact shall be eligible for a grant under this paragraph during—
the 2-year period beginning on the date on which an application for a grant under this paragraph with respect to the proposed compact is submitted to the Secretary; or
if the compact is formed before the date on which a grant under this paragraph is awarded in accordance with subclause (I), the initial 2 years of operation of the compact.

children.heading: Requirements.—
children.text: To be eligible to receive a grant under this paragraph, a multi-State freight compact or the applicable States seeking to form a multi-State freight compact shall—
submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require;
provide a non-Federal match equal to not less than 25 percent of the operating costs of the multi-State freight compact; and
commit to establishing a multi-State freight corridor advisory committee under subsection (c)(1) during the initial 2-year period of operation of the compact.

children.heading: In general.—
children.text: The Secretary may award a grant to multi-State freight compacts that are not eligible to receive a grant under paragraph (2) for operations costs in an amount of not more than $1,000,000.

children.heading: Requirements.—
children.text: To be eligible to receive a grant under this paragraph, a multi-State freight compact shall—
submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require;
provide a non-Federal match of not less than 50 percent of the operating costs of the compact; and
demonstrate that the compact has established a multi-State freight corridor advisory committee under subsection (c)(1).

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
children.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary $5,000,000 for each fiscal year to carry out this subsection.

notes.heading: Prior Provisions
notes.text: A prior section 70204 was renumbered section 70206 of this title.

ancestors.heading: MULTIMODAL FREIGHT TRANSPORTATION PLANNING AND INFORMATION
